text:
ana: Heads-up: saw strange behavior in go-sampleapp logs — request id shows up fine in first INFO line then later lines show "[redacted]" instead of the id. Repro attached.

diego: can you paste the snippet + env?

ana: oops my bad, name is ana. snippet: 
```
2026-10-05T09:21:05Z INFO http: start req_id=go-77 path=/v1/predict
2026-10-05T09:21:05Z INFO model: calling model req_id=[redacted] tokens=34
2026-10-05T09:21:05Z INFO http: done req_id=[redacted] status=200
```

ana: env: REDWOOD_GO_SDK=0.7.1, OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext, REDWOOD_REDACT_HEADERS="authorization,x-forwarded-for,x-request-id", REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info

rachel: interesting — Go SDK has separate otel hook that redacts headers and a logging middleware that picks up request id from context. Could be a race where redaction runs after logging middleware changes the context to the redacted value.

diego: I remember a change that canonicalized header names and wrote back sanitized values into the request object for performance. That could explain in-place mutation. We should never write back a redacted value into the propagated context key.

ana: yep, if the redactor sets header "x-request-id"->"[redacted]" before we read the header into ctx, then ctx gets redacted value. But in my repro the first line has id then later lines redacted, so looks like middleware reads early, then something else overwrites context later.

rachel: could be our tracer injection step. Otel->exporter might apply redaction to outgoing headers and mutate the same map used by request context. Go maps are reference types so copying is important.

diego: workaround: set REDWOOD_LOG_REDACT=false or remove x-request-id from REDWOOD_REDACT_HEADERS. Not great. I'll open INF-3378.

ci-bot: INF-3378 created by diego  https://redwood.company/infra/INF-3378

diego: fix plan: make redaction create a shallow copy of http.Header before mutating, and ensure logging middleware derives req_id from contextvars that we populate from the original header value at earliest entry point. Add unit test that asserts subsequent log lines preserve req_id even with redaction enabled.

rachel: also add an integration test for otel propagators variations (tracecontext vs b3) so we don't accidentally redact propagation headers when customers rely on them.

ana: thanks. PR would be great. I'll add the failing snippet to the ticket to help reproduce.

diego: will push a small patch and tag @rachel @ana for review; target micro patch release once CI is green.

ci-bot: RDW-RELEASE-934 created for INF-3378

rachel: we should also update the sampleapp README with a short troubleshooting note: if request ids disappear, check REDWOOD_REDACT_HEADERS and prefer explicit x- prefixes.

ana: noted and added to ticket. Thanks all.
